Here are the exact answers, sourced directly from your organisation's mandatory standards:

---

## Access Log Retention — `GLD-STD-002@1`, §3.1

The retention table in clause 3.1 states:

> **"Access log — 18 months — Security"**

Access logs must be retained for **18 months**, owned by the Security team. Clause 3.2 adds a critical obligation:

> **"Data held beyond its retention period is a reportable control failure."**

So the duty runs in both directions — logs must be kept for at least 18 months, and must be destroyed after that window closes.

---

## Soft-Deletes — `GLD-STD-002@1`, §4.1.1

The exact clause is:

> **"4.1.1 Deletion must be irreversible; a soft-delete flag does not satisfy this standard."**

This is unambiguous: using a soft-delete (e.g. an `IsDeleted = true` column) does **not** constitute destruction under this standard. Clause 4.1.2 reinforces this:

> **"4.1.2 Backups containing expired data must be rotated out within one backup cycle."**

---

## Practical implications for any code review

| Scenario | Status under `GLD-STD-002@1` |
|---|---|
| Setting `IsDeleted = true` on a record past its retention period | ❌ **Non-compliant** — not irreversible deletion |
| Archiving to cold storage indefinitely | ❌ **Non-compliant** — data held beyond period is a reportable control failure |
| Permanently removing the row + rotating backups | ✅ Compliant |
| Not declaring a data class before go-live | ❌ Treated as Customer PII (7 years after closure) |
